requirements.text: Without scrolling, the modal says the user is out of credits and that this is why their action stopped.
Gold is the visually recommended path, and Pro is still visible and purchasable.
The Pro-vs-Gold comparison is expressed in credits (5,000 vs 50,000), not only in features.
Both prices are shown: Pro $240/year and Gold $1,200/year, annual.
The modal can be dismissed by the close control, and dismissing returns the user to what they were doing.
A user who will not pay can see what they can still do on zero credits.
Pressing a plan CTA shows a pending state on that CTA and makes both CTAs non-interactive.
If checkout cannot be reached, an inline message with a retry appears and the modal stays dismissible.
The plan the user is currently on is visible, not implied.
What happens after the primary action is stated before it is pressed.
Copy says what the user gets, not what the system does; no congratulating the user on usage, no implication the credits were a trial.
Share of blocked users who purchase within 24 hours, versus the current pricing modal.
requirements.reason: an outcome measured in the warehouse weeks after launch, not a property of the screen

requirements.text: Shown at most once per user per 7 days.
requirements.reason: frequency capping is server-side eligibility logic; nothing about the rendered screen can evidence it
